name: Pye Records
ownershipStory: A UK label run as an arm of the Pye electronics company, and the label the Kinks signed to in 1964. Pye's contract terms and royalty accounting became a lasting grievance for Ray Davies, part of why the band spent much of the mid-1960s in business disputes even as their singles charted. Exact founding and closing dates for the label are not confirmed here and are left null rather than guessed.
hook: Signed the Kinks and then spent years disputing what it owed them.

blurb.age7: This company put out the Kinks' records, but argued with them a lot about money.
blurb.age13: Pye Records signed the Kinks in 1964. The band had hit after hit, but arguments with Pye over money and rights took up a lot of their time and energy in those years.
blurb.adult: Pye's relationship with the Kinks is a period-typical case of a British Invasion-era label extracting long-term value from a band whose control over royalties and publishing lagged well behind their commercial success.
